api_tests.tool: Django test framework (APITestCase) against live Postgres/Neon
api_tests.note: 148s for 19 simple tests is itself a finding — see performance.network_latency

security_findings.title: No rate limiting on login endpoint
security_findings.impact: Unlimited password-guessing attempts against any account. 15 wrong-password attempts in 12.25s, zero throttling (no 429 response ever seen).
security_findings.recommendation: Add DRF throttling (AnonRateThrottle/ScopedRateThrottle) or django-axes on the login view.

security_findings.title: DEBUG=True leaks full tracebacks on unhandled server errors
security_findings.impact: A real 500 (observed firsthand during Phase 1's MongoDB connection failure) returns full Python tracebacks, file paths, and settings values to the client.
security_findings.recommendation: DEBUG must be False before any real deployment; add DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS + a custom 500 handler.

security_findings.title: No Content-Security-Policy header
security_findings.impact: No defense-in-depth against XSS beyond React's own output escaping.
security_findings.recommendation: Add django-csp with a policy scoped to this app's actual asset origins.

security_findings.title: DEBUG=True technical 404 page reveals attempted URL pattern
security_findings.impact: Minor reconnaissance aid; same root cause and same fix as SEC-04b.

security_findings.title: Anonymous endpoints (register/login) have no CSRF check
security_findings.component: DRF SessionAuthentication (framework default, not app misconfiguration)
security_findings.impact: "Login CSRF" — a forged cross-site request could make a victim register/log into an attacker-known account. No sensitive data is at risk purely from that.
security_findings.recommendation: By design in DRF; not treated as an app defect. Documented for awareness.

security_passed.title: Authenticated writes correctly reject missing CSRF token (403)
CORS correctly refuses to echo an untrusted Origin
Baseline hardening headers present (nosniff, X-Frame-Options DENY, Referrer-Policy, COOP)
Session cookie is HttpOnly (confirmed via raw Set-Cookie header)

reliability_findings.title: Malformed JSON body → clean 400, not a 500
Oversized field (10,000 chars) rejected by serializer validation before reaching the DB
5 concurrent identical-username registrations → exactly 1 succeeded, DB unique constraint held under a real race

tool_comparison.locust: Python-native, easy to script the exact multi-step user flow (register→login→CRUD) with real state (note IDs) carried between requests.
tool_comparison.k6: JS-based, built-in percentile/threshold reporting out of the box (http_req_failed rate<0.01 as a pass/fail gate), lighter resource footprint.

performance.network_latency: Every DB operation is a real network round-trip to Neon (not localhost) — this shows up everywhere: the 19-test suite took 148s, and it's the root contributor to auth latency under load.

load_stages.notes: k6 script measures the whole flow per request, not split by endpoint like Locust's per-name stats — independently confirms the same overall latency scale as the Locust 50-user run.

bottleneck.title: Auth endpoints (register/login) scale far worse than notes CRUD under concurrency
bottleneck.root_cause: PBKDF2 password hashing is CPU-bound and, on Django's single-process dev server, serializes under Python's GIL. Notes CRUD is I/O-bound (waiting on the Neon network round-trip) and releases the GIL while waiting, so many can be in flight concurrently — auth requests queue behind each other's hashing work instead.
bottleneck.evidence: Notes latency stayed ~840-1150ms flat across 10→100 users. Auth latency: 2.9s → 3.0s → 6.1s across the same progression — non-linear growth exactly where CPU-bound work would queue.
bottleneck.caveat: This was measured against `manage.py runserver` (explicitly not a production server). A real deployment (Gunicorn, multiple worker processes) would spread hashing across processes/cores instead of one GIL — re-measuring after containerization (Phase 3) is the honest next step, not assumed away here.
bottleneck.reliability_note: Zero failed requests at every stage tested (10/50/100 users) — the app got slower under load, it did not break.

findings.title: ForeignKey(owner) auto-indexed by Django, FK constraint enforced by Postgres
findings.evidence: psql \d notes_note shows notes_note_owner_id_8dafc06d btree index and a real FK constraint to auth_user(id).

findings.title: Test database teardown fails against Neon's pooled (PgBouncer) connection
findings.evidence: psycopg.errors.ObjectInUse: database "test_neondb" is being accessed by other users — DROP DATABASE fails, test_neondb left orphaned (does not affect the real neondb data).
findings.recommendation: Use a direct (non-pooled) connection string for admin operations like `manage.py test`/`migrate`, reserving the pooled endpoint for the running app's normal traffic.

devops.reason: Docker/CI/CD is Phase 3 scope by the project's own plan — testing containers/pipelines that don't exist yet would test nothing real. See DEFERRED_TESTS.md.
